topics.title: Introduction to Java
topics.summary: History, JVM/JRE/JDK architecture, platform independence, write once run anywhere principle, and first Java program.
topics.definition: Java is a class-based, object-oriented, concurrent, secure, and general-purpose programming language designed to let application developers write once, run anywhere (WORA).
topics.detailedExplanation: Java source code (.java) is compiled by javac into intermediate bytecode (.class). This platform-independent bytecode is executed by the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The JVM uses a ClassLoader, Bytecode Verifier, and Execution Engine (comprising an Interpreter and Just-In-Time JIT Compiler). The Java Runtime Environment (JRE) bundles the JVM with standard core libraries, while the Java Development Kit (JDK) includes the JRE plus development tools like javac, jdb, and javadoc.
practicalApplications: Big data processing engines (Apache Spark, Hadoop)

codeExamples.title: HelloWorld.java
codeExamples.explanation: public gives visibility from anywhere; static allows JVM to invoke without instantiating the class; void indicates no return value; String[] args takes command-line arguments.

complexityAnalysis.explanation: Execution of main entry point takes constant time.

commonMistakes: Mismatched file name and public class name
Forgetting static in main method
Misunderstanding that Java is pass-by-value strictly

interviewQuestions.question: Why is Java platform independent, but JVM is platform dependent?
interviewQuestions.answer: Java source code is compiled into bytecode which runs on any JVM regardless of OS. However, each operating system requires a custom JVM implementation tailored to that OS machine code.
interviewQuestions.tips: Highlight the distinction between .class bytecode and native machine code.

examQuestions.question: Explain the internal architecture of JVM with a neat diagram.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Cover ClassLoader subsystem, Memory Areas (Method Area, Heap, JVM Stack, PC Register, Native Method Stack), Execution Engine (Interpreter, JIT Compiler, Garbage Collector), and JNI.

practiceExercises: Install JDK and compile a program from the terminal using javac and java.
Pass command-line arguments to compute their sum.
revisionNotes: JDK = JRE + Development Tools
JRE = JVM + Class Libraries
Source code -> javac -> .class bytecode -> JVM (JIT/Interpreter) -> Machine Code

topics.title: Variables and Data Types
topics.summary: Primitive data types, sizes, ranges, wrapper classes, reference types, type casting, and variable scopes.
topics.definition: A variable is a named memory location used to store data, while a data type defines the size, range, and layout of values that can be stored.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java has 8 primitive types: byte (8-bit), short (16-bit), int (32-bit), long (64-bit), float (32-bit IEEE 754), double (64-bit IEEE 754), char (16-bit Unicode UTF-16), and boolean. All numeric types are signed. Reference types hold addresses of objects allocated on the heap. Autoboxing automatically converts primitives to Wrapper classes (e.g., int to Integer). Widening casting is implicit, while narrowing casting requires explicit casts.
typesAndClassifications: Primitive Data Types (Integral, Floating-point, Char, Boolean)
Non-Primitive / Reference Data Types (Classes, Interfaces, Arrays, Enums)
importantConcepts: Implicit widening vs Explicit narrowing casting
practicalApplications: Financial arithmetic requiring BigDecimal over double

codeExamples.title: TypeCasting.java
codeExamples.explanation: Shows implicit widening and explicit narrowing with precision loss.

complexityAnalysis.explanation: Variable allocations on stack are fixed size.

commonMistakes: Using double/float for exact financial calculations instead of BigDecimal
Integer overflow without exception (wrap-around in two's complement)

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between Integer.valueOf() and new Integer()?
interviewQuestions.answer: Integer.valueOf() utilizes an internal cache for values from -128 to 127, avoiding redundant heap allocations, whereas new Integer() always allocates a new object on heap.
interviewQuestions.tips: Mention the IntegerCache mechanism.

examQuestions.question: Differentiate between primitive data types and reference data types in Java.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Tabulate: memory location (stack vs heap), default values, nullability, method invocation, and wrapper classes.

practiceExercises: Demonstrate integer overflow when adding Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1
Benchmark primitive int[] vs List<Integer> memory consumption.
revisionNotes: 8 primitives: byte(1B), short(2B), int(4B), long(8B), float(4B), double(8B), char(2B), boolean
Primitive values live on Stack; objects on Heap

topics.title: Operators and Expressions
topics.summary: Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise, shift, ternary, and assignment operators, operator precedence and associativity.
topics.definition: Operators are special symbols that perform specific operations on one, two, or three operands and return a result.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java provides arithmetic (+, -, *, /, %), relational (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=), logical (&&, ||, !), bitwise (&, |, ^, ~), bit shift (<<, >>, >>>), and assignment operators. Short-circuit evaluation in && and || avoids evaluating the right operand if the left operand determines the outcome. Bitwise >>> performs an unsigned right shift filling high-order bits with zeroes.
practicalApplications: Fast bit manipulation for permissions and bitmasks

codeExamples.title: OperatorsDemo.java
codeExamples.code:
int a = 8; // 1000 in binary
int shifted = a >> 1; // 4 (0100)
boolean check = (a != 0) && (100 / a > 5); // Short-circuit safe
codeExamples.explanation: Right shift divides by 2; short-circuit operator prevents division by zero.

complexityAnalysis.explanation: CPU ALU instructions execute in 1-2 clock cycles.

commonMistakes: Confusing & and &&
Operator precedence misconceptions with + and ternary operator

interviewQuestions.question: How does >>> differ from >> in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: >> performs arithmetic right shift preserving sign bit; >>> performs logical right shift inserting 0 into leftmost position.
interviewQuestions.tips: Mention signed vs unsigned bit shifting.

examQuestions.question: Explain short-circuit operators with an example.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Demonstrate && skipping evaluation of second operand when first operand is false.

practiceExercises: Write a program to check if an integer is a power of 2 using bitwise operators in O(1).
revisionNotes: && and || short-circuit; & and | evaluate both sides
>> preserves sign, >>> shifts zero into sign position

topics.title: Conditional Statements
topics.summary: if, if-else, else-if ladder, nested if, traditional switch, switch expressions with yield, and pattern matching.
topics.definition: Conditional statements allow programs to choose different execution paths based on boolean evaluations.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java includes standard if/else branching and switch statements. In modern Java (Java 14+), switch expressions support comma-separated case labels, lambda arrows (->) that eliminate break statements, and the yield keyword to return values. Java 21+ adds pattern matching for switch, enabling type checks directly inside case branches.
importantConcepts: Pattern matching for switch in modern Java

codeExamples.title: ModernSwitch.java
codeExamples.explanation: Shows modern switch expression returning a value without break statements.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: O(1) table lookup or O(n) branching
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Switch compiles to tableswitch or lookupswitch bytecode.

commonMistakes: Missing break causing unintentional fall-through in legacy switch

interviewQuestions.question: How does the JVM optimize a switch statement?
interviewQuestions.answer: JVM compiles switch into either tableswitch (dense keys, O(1) jump table) or lookupswitch (sparse keys, O(log n) binary search table).
interviewQuestions.tips: Mention bytecode instructions tableswitch and lookupswitch.

examQuestions.question: Compare if-else ladder with switch-case statement.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Tabulate on readability, expression types supported, speed, and jump table optimization.

practiceExercises: Implement an HTTP status code classifier using switch expressions.
revisionNotes: Modern switch uses -> to eliminate fall-through
tableswitch is O(1); lookupswitch is O(log n)

topics.title: Loops and Iteration
topics.summary: for, while, do-while, enhanced for-each loop, break, continue, labeled statements.
topics.definition: Loops are control flow structures that repeatedly execute a block of code as long as a specified condition remains true.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java provides while (entry-controlled), do-while (exit-controlled, guarantees at least one execution), standard for loop (initialization; condition; increment), and enhanced for-each loop for Iterable collections and arrays. Labeled break and continue allow breaking out of outer nested loops.

codeExamples.title: LabeledLoops.java
codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates breaking out of outer loop directly from inner loop.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: O(n) or O(n^2)
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Determined by loop count and nesting.

commonMistakes: Modifying a Collection while iterating with enhanced for-each instead of using Iterator.remove()

interviewQuestions.question: What causes ConcurrentModificationException during iteration?
interviewQuestions.answer: Collections like ArrayList track modCount. When an enhanced for loop uses an Iterator, if the list is modified structurally without the Iterator methods, modCount != expectedModCount triggers the exception (fail-fast).
interviewQuestions.tips: Explain modCount and fail-fast behavior.

examQuestions.question: Differentiate between while and do-while loops with syntax.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Entry-controlled vs exit-controlled; condition check timing; guarantee of at least one iteration.

practiceExercises: Write a program using labeled break to find an item in a 2D matrix.
revisionNotes: while checks before execution; do-while checks after
Enhanced for loop uses Iterator under the hood

topics.title: Methods and Recursion
topics.summary: Method signature, return types, pass-by-value semantics, method overloading, varargs, and recursive call stacks.
topics.definition: A method is a reusable block of code that performs an operation, while recursion is a technique where a method calls itself to solve smaller subproblems.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java is strictly pass-by-value. When an object reference is passed, the reference address is copied by value. Method overloading means methods in the same class have the same name but different parameter lists. Recursion relies on the JVM call stack, where each activation record stores local variables and return addresses until the base condition is met; failure to reach the base case results in StackOverflowError.
importantConcepts: Recursion Base Case and Call Stack Frames

codeExamples.title: FactorialRecursion.java
codeExamples.explanation: Base case prevents infinite recursion; call stack collapses upon reaching n=1.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: O(n)
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Each recursive call allocates a stack frame.

commonMistakes: Believing Java passes objects by reference (it passes references by value)

interviewQuestions.question: Is Java pass-by-reference or pass-by-value?
interviewQuestions.answer: Java is strictly pass-by-value always. For primitives, the value itself is copied. For objects, the reference (memory address pointer) is copied by value.
interviewQuestions.tips: Illustrate by reassigning a parameter reference inside a method to show it does not affect caller.

examQuestions.question: What is method overloading? State its rules and write a program.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Must differ in parameter type, number, or order. Return type alone is insufficient.

practiceExercises: Write a recursive method to solve the Tower of Hanoi problem.
revisionNotes: Java is always pass-by-value
Recursion requires base condition to avoid StackOverflowError

topics.title: Arrays and Strings
topics.summary: 1D and multidimensional arrays, String immutability, String Constant Pool, StringBuilder, and StringBuffer.
topics.definition: Arrays are fixed-size sequential collections of elements of identical data type, while Strings in Java are immutable sequences of characters.
topics.detailedExplanation: Arrays are objects stored on the heap with contiguous memory allocation and zero-based indexing. Strings are immutable objects backed by the String Pool to conserve heap memory. Modifying a String creates a new object in heap. StringBuilder is mutable and non-thread-safe (high performance), whereas StringBuffer is synchronized (thread-safe).
importantConcepts: Immutability benefits: Security, Caching, Thread safety
practicalApplications: String concatenation in tight loops with StringBuilder

codeExamples.title: StringPoolDemo.java
codeExamples.code:
String s1 = "Java"; // SCP
String s2 = "Java"; // Points to same literal in SCP
String s3 = new String("Java"); // Explicit Heap allocation
System.out.println(s1 == s2); // true (same reference)
System.out.println(s1 == s3); // false (different objects)
System.out.println(s1.equals(s3)); // true (content comparison)
codeExamples.explanation: Shows reference equality (==) vs content equality (.equals()).

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Array access O(1); String concat in loop without StringBuilder O(n^2)
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Array indexing uses pointer offset math.

commonMistakes: Using == instead of .equals() for String comparison
Concatenating strings inside a loop using +

interviewQuestions.question: Why is String immutable in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Security (class loading, DB credentials), String Constant Pool caching, thread safety without synchronization, and hashcode caching for HashMaps.
interviewQuestions.tips: Mention HashCode caching.

examQuestions.question: Differentiate between String, StringBuffer, and StringBuilder.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Tabulate mutability, thread safety, synchronization overhead, and speed.

practiceExercises: Implement an in-place string reversal algorithm and check for palindrome.
revisionNotes: String is immutable; stored in String Constant Pool
Use StringBuilder for single-threaded concatenation; StringBuffer for multi-threaded

topics.title: Object-Oriented Programming Principles
topics.summary: The 4 pillars of OOP: Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, and Polymorphism with design paradigms.
topics.definition: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on the concept of objects containing data fields and operating methods.
topics.detailedExplanation: OOP structures software around real-world entities. The four primary pillars are: Encapsulation (binding data and methods while hiding internal state via private fields and getters/setters), Abstraction (hiding implementation complexity and exposing essential interfaces via abstract classes and interfaces), Inheritance (reusing attributes and behaviors across hierarchies using extends), and Polymorphism (ability of an entity to take multiple forms at compile-time or runtime).

codeExamples.title: EncapsulationDemo.java
codeExamples.explanation: Protects balance from direct invalid modifications.

complexityAnalysis.explanation: Encapsulated field accesses take constant time.

commonMistakes: Exposing mutable internal objects via getters without defensive copying

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between Abstraction and Encapsulation?
interviewQuestions.answer: Abstraction focuses on "what" an object does (hiding complexity), while Encapsulation focuses on "how" to hide internal state and data within boundaries.
interviewQuestions.tips: Abstraction at design level; Encapsulation at implementation level.

examQuestions.question: Discuss the 4 pillars of OOP with suitable Java code illustrations.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Dedicate one section and code snippet to each: Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism.

practiceExercises: Design a PaymentProcessing system using abstraction and encapsulation.
revisionNotes: Encapsulation = Data Hiding
Abstraction = Complexity Hiding
Inheritance = Code Reuse
Polymorphism = Multiple Forms

topics.title: Classes and Objects
topics.summary: Constructors (default, parameterized, copy), this keyword, static members, and object lifecycle.
topics.definition: A class is a blueprint or template from which individual objects are created; an object is a runtime instance of a class with state and behavior.
topics.detailedExplanation: When an object is created with new, memory is allocated on the heap, instance variables are initialized with default values, and the constructor executes to initialize user state. The this keyword refers to the current object instance. Static fields and methods belong to the class itself rather than any individual instance and reside in the Metaspace/Method Area.
importantConcepts: Static vs Instance variables and methods
Object lifecycle and Garbage Collection eligibility
practicalApplications: Utility classes (e.g. java.lang.Math) with static members

codeExamples.title: Student.java
codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates instance initialization and shared static counter.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Instantiation O(1)
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Heap object allocation overhead.

commonMistakes: Calling an instance method from a static context without an object reference

interviewQuestions.question: Can static methods access instance variables in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: No, static methods belong to the class and execute without an active instance reference (this is not available in static context).
interviewQuestions.tips: Explain why "this" does not exist in static context.

examQuestions.question: Explain constructor chaining in Java with an example.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Show this(...) calling another constructor in the same class and super(...) calling parent constructor.

practiceExercises: Create an immutable Person class with builder pattern.
revisionNotes: Class = Blueprint; Object = Instance on Heap
Static belongs to Class; Non-static belongs to Instance

topics.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
topics.summary: Single, multilevel, hierarchical inheritance, super keyword, method overriding, dynamic method dispatch, and runtime polymorphism.
topics.definition: Inheritance is a mechanism where a new class acquires properties of an existing class, and polymorphism allows one interface to control multiple implementations.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java supports single inheritance for classes (avoiding the diamond problem). The super keyword invokes parent constructors or overridden methods. Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides a specific implementation of a method declared in its superclass with the exact same signature. At runtime, Java resolves the overridden method based on the actual object type via Dynamic Method Dispatch using the vtable.
practicalApplications: Extending framework base classes (e.g. Spring Security / Android Activity)

codeExamples.title: PolymorphismDemo.java
codeExamples.explanation: Runtime method lookup calls Dog's makeSound method.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Method dispatch O(1) via virtual method table (vtable)
complexityAnalysis.explanation: JVM vtable lookup overhead.

commonMistakes: Attempting multiple inheritance with classes instead of interfaces
Overriding private or static methods (static methods are shadowed, not overridden)

interviewQuestions.question: Can we override static methods in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: No, static methods are resolved at compile-time based on the reference type (method hiding), not dynamic dispatch at runtime.
interviewQuestions.tips: Distinguish method hiding from method overriding.

examQuestions.question: What is dynamic method dispatch? Explain with a code example.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Explain parent reference pointing to child object and runtime resolution of overridden methods.

practiceExercises: Design a Shape hierarchy with Circle, Rectangle, Triangle and calculate area polymorphically.
revisionNotes: Inheritance uses "extends"
Dynamic method dispatch resolves methods at runtime via actual heap object

topics.title: Interfaces and Abstraction
topics.summary: Abstract classes vs interfaces, default methods, static methods in interfaces, private interface methods, and multiple inheritance via interfaces.
topics.definition: An interface is a contract specifying methods a class must implement, enabling multiple inheritance of type and decoupled architecture.
topics.detailedExplanation: Abstract classes can hold state (instance fields) and constructors, while interfaces traditionally defined purely abstract method signatures. Since Java 8, interfaces support default methods (enabling backward compatibility) and static methods. Since Java 9, private helper methods are permitted in interfaces. A class can implement multiple interfaces, allowing polymorphism across unrelated hierarchies.
importantConcepts: Resolving diamond problem with default methods
practicalApplications: Decoupling API contracts from implementations (JDBC interfaces)

codeExamples.title: PaymentGateway.java
codeExamples.explanation: Shows contract method and default implementation.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Interface dispatch O(1) via itable
complexityAnalysis.explanation: JVM itable lookup.

commonMistakes: Creating an abstract class when an interface is sufficient for defining contracts

interviewQuestions.question: When should you use an abstract class versus an interface?
interviewQuestions.answer: Use an abstract class when classes share code, non-static state, or access modifiers. Use an interface when defining a public contract for unrelated classes or when multiple inheritance of type is needed.
interviewQuestions.tips: Contrast "is-a" stateful relationship vs "can-do" contractual capability.

examQuestions.question: Differentiate between abstract class and interface in Java with examples.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Tabulate on: multiple inheritance, instance variables, constructors, speed, and default methods.

practiceExercises: Create a Repository interface with CRUD methods and an InMemoryRepository implementation.
revisionNotes: Interfaces achieve 100% abstraction (prior to default methods)
A class extends one class, but can implement many interfaces

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.summary: Throwable hierarchy, checked vs unchecked exceptions, try-catch-finally, try-with-resources (AutoCloseable), custom exceptions, and best practices.
topics.definition: Exception handling is a mechanism to handle runtime errors gracefully, maintaining regular application flow without unexpected crashes.
topics.detailedExplanation: The Throwable hierarchy branches into Error (serious system failures like OutOfMemoryError) and Exception. Exceptions branch into Checked (must be caught or declared in throws clause, subclassing Exception) and Unchecked (subclassing RuntimeException, like NullPointerException or IllegalArgumentException). Java 7 introduced try-with-resources, which automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable.

codeExamples.title: TryWithResources.java
codeExamples.explanation: br is closed automatically even if an exception occurs.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Normal path zero cost; exception throw O(stack depth) to generate stack trace
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Filling stack trace has overhead.

commonMistakes: Swallowing exceptions in empty catch blocks
Catching generic Throwable or Exception instead of specific subclasses

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
interviewQuestions.answer: Checked exceptions are verified at compile time and require explicit handling (catch or throws). Unchecked exceptions occur at runtime (subclasses of RuntimeException) and indicate programmer bugs or unexpected conditions.
interviewQuestions.tips: Provide examples: IOException vs NullPointerException.

examQuestions.question: Explain the exception hierarchy in Java and write a custom exception class.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Draw Throwable tree; write CustomNotFoundException extending RuntimeException.

practiceExercises: Write a custom InsufficientFundsException and throw it in a withdraw method.
revisionNotes: Throwable -> Error, Exception
Exception -> RuntimeException (Unchecked) & Checked Exceptions
try-with-resources guarantees closing of AutoCloseable

topics.title: Collections Framework
topics.summary: List (ArrayList, LinkedList), Set (HashSet, TreeSet, LinkedHashSet), Map (HashMap, TreeMap), Queue, Deque, equals and hashCode contract.
topics.definition: The Java Collections Framework is a unified architecture for representing and manipulating collections of objects, providing interfaces, implementations, and algorithms.
topics.detailedExplanation: The hierarchy roots at Iterable -> Collection -> List, Set, Queue. Map is a separate hierarchy for key-value pairs. ArrayList uses a dynamic resizable array (amortized O(1) append). LinkedList is a doubly-linked list. HashSet is backed by HashMap (O(1) average lookup). TreeSet uses a Red-Black tree (O(log n) ordered operations). HashMap uses an array of buckets; on collision, entries form a linked list, transforming into a balanced red-black tree (TREEIFY_THRESHOLD = 8).
importantConcepts: HashMap collision resolution (Buckets, linked nodes, red-black tree)

codeExamples.title: CollectionsDemo.java
codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates HashMap key-value association and lambda iteration.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: HashMap get/put: O(1) average, O(log n) worst; TreeSet: O(log n)
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Amortized resizing and hashing operations.

commonMistakes: Overriding equals() without overriding hashCode(), breaking HashMap lookups
Modifying keys while stored in a HashSet/HashMap

interviewQuestions.question: How does HashMap handle collisions internally in Java 8+?
interviewQuestions.answer: Keys hashing to the same bucket index form a linked list. When bucket size exceeds 8 and total capacity >= 64, the linked list converts into a Red-Black tree (TreeNode), improving worst-case search from O(n) to O(log n).
interviewQuestions.tips: Mention TREEIFY_THRESHOLD (8) and UNTREEIFY_THRESHOLD (6).

examQuestions.question: Explain the internal working of HashMap in Java with a diagram.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Detail hashing, bucket index calculation, collision chaining, and treeification in Java 8.

practiceExercises: Sort a List of Employees by salary descending and then by name using Comparator.
revisionNotes: ArrayList: O(1) random access; LinkedList: O(1) insertions at ends
HashMap: O(1) average; converts to Red-Black tree at 8 collisions

topics.title: Generics
topics.summary: Type safety, type erasure, generic classes, generic methods, bounded type parameters, and wildcards (? extends T, ? super T).
topics.definition: Generics enable types (classes and interfaces) to be parameters when defining classes, interfaces, and methods, enforcing compile-time type safety.
topics.detailedExplanation: Before Generics (pre-Java 5), collections held Objects, requiring manual casts prone to ClassCastException. Generics provide compile-time verification. At compile time, the Java compiler applies Type Erasure, replacing generic parameters with Object (or their first bound) and inserting appropriate casts in the bytecode to preserve backward compatibility. Upper-bounded wildcards (? extends T) provide read access; lower-bounded wildcards (? super T) allow writing (PECS principle: Producer Extends, Consumer Super).
importantConcepts: Compile-time type safety without runtime performance penalty
practicalApplications: Generic response wrappers in Web APIs (e.g., ApiResponse<T>)

codeExamples.title: GenericBox.java
codeExamples.explanation: Box can store any specified type safely without manual casting.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Compile-time validation O(1) runtime
complexityAnalysis.explanation: No runtime overhead due to type erasure.

commonMistakes: Attempting to create generic arrays (new T[10] is invalid due to type erasure)
Using primitive types as generic arguments directly (use Wrapper types)

interviewQuestions.question: What is Type Erasure and what are its implications?
interviewQuestions.answer: Type erasure removes all generic type information during compilation to maintain binary compatibility with older Java versions. Consequently, generic type information is unavailable at runtime via reflection unless preserved in superclass signatures.
interviewQuestions.tips: Mention why instanceof List<String> is forbidden.

examQuestions.question: Explain the PECS guideline with a code example.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Producer Extends (read only), Consumer Super (write only); show Collection copy method.

practiceExercises: Implement a generic Stack<T> class with push, pop, and peek.
revisionNotes: Generics ensure compile-time type safety
PECS: Producer Extends, Consumer Super
JVM erases types to Object or upper bound at runtime

topics.title: Multithreading and Concurrency
topics.summary: Thread lifecycle, Runnable vs Callable, synchronization, volatile, deadlock, ExecutorService, and modern Virtual Threads (Project Loom).
topics.definition: Multithreading is a programming capability that allows multiple threads of execution to run concurrently within a single process to maximize CPU utilization.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java supports multithreading via Thread class, Runnable, and Callable interfaces. Thread states include NEW, RUNNABLE, BLOCKED, WAITING, TIMED_WAITING, and TERMINATED. Synchronization (using synchronized keyword or ReentrantLock) prevents race conditions by acquiring monitor locks. Volatile guarantees memory visibility across CPU caches. Java 5 introduced java.util.concurrent (ExecutorService, CountDownLatch, ConcurrentHashMap). Java 21 introduced Virtual Threads (lightweight threads managed by JVM rather than OS).
practicalApplications: High-throughput HTTP servers handling thousands of concurrent requests
Asynchronous background computation and I/O polling

codeExamples.title: ExecutorDemo.java
codeExamples.explanation: Runs asynchronous task inside managed thread pool.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Concurrency reduces wall-clock latency
complexityAnalysis.spaceComplexity: Platform thread: ~1MB stack; Virtual thread: ~few hundred bytes
complexityAnalysis.explanation: Virtual threads drastically reduce memory footprint.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to call shutdown() on ExecutorService causing JVM to hang
Deadlock by acquiring locks in inconsistent order

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between volatile and synchronized in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: volatile guarantees visibility of variable changes across threads by reading/writing directly to main memory, but does not guarantee atomicity (e.g. count++ is not thread-safe). synchronized guarantees both visibility and mutual exclusion (atomicity).
interviewQuestions.tips: Highlight compound operations like count++.

examQuestions.question: What is deadlock? State the four necessary conditions and how to prevent it.
examQuestions.solutionGuide: Mutual exclusion, Hold and wait, No preemption, Circular wait; lock ordering technique.

practiceExercises: Implement the Producer-Consumer problem using wait() and notifyAll().
revisionNotes: volatile = visibility; synchronized = visibility + atomicity
Virtual threads allow millions of concurrent tasks with minimal memory

topics.title: File Handling and I/O
topics.summary: Byte streams vs Character streams, Buffered I/O, Serialization, and modern Java NIO.2 (Files, Path).
topics.definition: File handling enables Java programs to read and write data persistently to disk storage using streams and channels.
topics.detailedExplanation: Java I/O is divided into Byte Streams (InputStream, OutputStream for binary data) and Character Streams (Reader, Writer for 16-bit Unicode text). Buffered streams wrap raw streams to minimize expensive system calls. Java 7 introduced NIO.2 (java.nio.file.Path and Files), providing non-blocking operations, stream transformations, and clean file system utilities. Serialization converts an object into a byte stream for storage or network transport.

codeExamples.title: ModernNIO.java
codeExamples.explanation: Clean one-line file writing and reading using modern Java NIO.2.

complexityAnalysis.timeComplexity: Sequential I/O O(n)

topics.title: Java Database Connectivity (JDBC)
topics.summary: JDBC architecture, Driver, Connection, Statement vs PreparedStatement, CallableStatement, ResultSet, and Connection Pooling.
topics.definition: JDBC is a standard Java API that connects Java applications to relational database management systems and executes SQL statements.
topics.detailedExplanation: JDBC workflow involves loading the JDBC driver, obtaining a Connection via DriverManager or DataSource, creating a PreparedStatement with parameterized queries, executing the query to get a ResultSet, processing rows via rs.next(), and closing resources. PreparedStatement precompiles SQL queries on the database server, enhancing performance and completely preventing SQL Injection attacks. Production systems use Connection Pools (e.g., HikariCP) to reuse expensive database sockets.
typesAndClassifications: JDBC Driver Types: Type 1 (ODBC Bridge), Type 2 (Native API), Type 3 (Network Protocol), Type 4 (Pure Java Thin Driver)
importantConcepts: SQL Injection prevention via parameter binding
practicalApplications: Relational persistence in Spring Data JDBC

complexityAnalysis.explanation: Cursor fetches rows in batches.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is PreparedStatement faster and safer than Statement in JDBC?
interviewQuestions.answer: PreparedStatement is precompiled by the database engine and can be reused with different parameters, reducing parsing time. It automatically escapes input parameters, neutralizing SQL injection attacks.
interviewQuestions.tips: Always mention SQL injection security first.

topics.summary: Comprehensive compilation of core Java interview questions, tricky edge cases, and architectural discussions.

topics.detailedExplanation: Top technical interview questions evaluate candidate depth in JVM memory management (Heap, Stack, Metaspace), Garbage Collection mechanisms (G1, ZGC, generational hypothesis), Stream API internals, Optional pattern, and concurrent constructs. Candidates must explain internal trade-offs clearly with code examples.
importantConcepts: Generational Garbage Collection (Young Gen, Old Gen, Eden, Survivor)
